profile.shape: Event stream with weekly aggregated category-geography records

errors.error: Artifact workbook daemon timed out on the first import attempt.
errors.resolution: Retried with a longer daemon startup timeout.
errors.consequence: No analysis would have been produced.

errors.error: A whole-sheet inspect returned a truncated value payload.
errors.resolution: Read the worksheet through range.values and asserted 7,598 data rows.
errors.consequence: A partial dataset could have been mistaken for the full workbook.

errors.error: Using the 2025 week ending 30 August produced totals that did not match the analyst comparison period.
errors.caught_by: Cross-check against the supplied assessment totals.
errors.resolution: Matched 34 weekly observations: 4 Jan to 23 Aug 2025 against 3 Jan to 29 Aug 2026.
errors.consequence: Year-on-year change rates would have been understated.

errors.error: The notes list 400 fatalities for 2025 Cameroon attacks, while the workbook sums 399 for the Attack sub-event.
errors.resolution: The publication uses the workbook value for the sub-event and retains 400 only for the broader violence-against-civilians event type.
errors.consequence: A category-level fatality statement would have been off by one.

falsification.overturn: A refreshed event-level extract shows the 2026 abduction increase is primarily a coding or deduplication artifact rather than additional incidents.
Actor-attributed event data shows the apparent mix of mob, battle, abduction and air activity is generated by one coherent campaign rather than multiple mechanisms.
A longer ADMIN1 panel removes the negative association between coercive share and lethality or reverses its sign after within-region controls.
Later 2026 weeks show the current high-burden regions reverting rapidly toward baseline while other ADMIN1 units sustain the escalation.
